title: Biomimicry Principles in Architecture for Promoting Healthy Buildings: An Analysis of Relevant Literatures

findings.antecedent: Biological imitation strategies (biomimicry) in building design
findings.consequent: Wellness (human comfort, physical, mental, social well-being)
findings.quote: This research is about applying biological imitation strategies in building design to see wellness fostered in the light of nature's adaptive and efficient capabilities

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (termite mound inspired passive cooling systems)
findings.quote: Some notable examples include passive cooling systems (inspired by termite mounds)

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (lotus leaf inspired self-cleaning surfaces)
findings.quote: or self-cleaning surfaces (imitating lotus leaves)

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (rainforest canopy inspired spatial designs for light and air openings)
findings.consequent: Improved daylighting, ventilation, indoor air quality
findings.quote: or spatial designs like those receiving light and air openings from rainforest canopies' tiered structure

findings.antecedent: Biomimetic architecture
findings.quote: buildings developed through this approach not only stand as sustainable structures but additionally support user comfortability.

findings.antecedent: Good physical environment (indoor air quality, thermal comfort, acoustics)
findings.quote: Research has demonstrated that the physical environment, including indoor air quality (IAQ), thermal comfort, and acoustics, plays a significant role in the physical health of individuals residing or working within these spaces.

findings.antecedent: Good lighting, color schemes, and views
findings.quote: the psychological well-being of occupants is also a priority, with factors such as lighting, color schemes, and views significantly impacting mental health (Liu et al., 2023).

findings.antecedent: Accessibility to green spaces (core principle of biomimetic architecture)
findings.consequent: Physical activity, overall health and well-being among building occupants
findings.quote: The accessibility to green spaces, a core principle of biomimetic architecture, encourages physical activity among building occupants, thereby contributing to their overall health and well-being.

findings.antecedent: Biomimetic design regulating circadian rhythms
findings.consequent: Physical health, quality of sleep, general health
findings.quote: Furthermore, the emphasis on creating environments that regulate circadian rhythms underscores the commitment of biomimetic design to the physical health of individuals, enhancing the quality of sleep and, by extension, their general health (Hower et al., 2018).

findings.antecedent: Biomimetic strategies (passive cooling, natural ventilation, water harvesting)
findings.quote: Biomimetic strategies such as passive cooling, natural ventilation, and water harvesting can significantly reduce a building's environmental impact.

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (studying natural forms for strength, flexibility, load-bearing)
findings.quote: Biomimicry offers architects insights into optimizing building structures by studying the strength, flexibility, and load-bearing capabilities of natural forms.

findings.antecedent: Proper ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC with filters, UV lights, bipolar ionization)
findings.consequent: Indoor air quality, reduced biological/chemical pollutants
findings.quote: Proper ventilation and air conditioning is crucial for maintaining indoor air quality. According to the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), indoor air can be 2-5 times more polluted than outdoor air. HVAC systems should include air filters (MERV 13 or higher as recommended by ASHRAE) to remove particulate matter, and may use technologies like UV lights or bipolar ionization to reduce biological and chemical pollutants (Ottney, 1993).

findings.antecedent: Controlled temperature (68-75°F) and humidity (30-60% RH)
findings.consequent: Occupant comfort, prevention of mold growth
findings.quote: Controlling temperature (68-75°F) and humidity (30-60% RH) is also important for occupant comfort and preventing mold growth (Wu & Wong, 2022).

findings.antecedent: VOCs from building materials
findings.quote: Building materials can off-gas volatile organic compounds (VOCs) like formaldehyde which are linked to respiratory issues and cancer risks.

findings.antecedent: Access to daylight and views to the outdoors
findings.quote: Access to daylight and views to the outdoors can improve mood, focus and sleep quality according to studies.

findings.antecedent: Excessive noise
findings.quote: Excessive noise can increase stress and negatively impact sleep and cognitive performance.

findings.antecedent: Green walls
findings.quote: Experiments in controlled environments reveal green walls' considerable promise as an acoustic insulator for architectural structures and that Rw15 dB and a 0.40 can be delivered with ease (Azkorra et al., 2015).

findings.antecedent: Biomimetic designs
findings.consequent: Lower operating costs, enhanced efficiency, sustainability
findings.quote: Biomimetic designs contribute to lower operating costs in buildings through several mechanisms that enhance efficiency and sustainability.

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (termite mound inspired ventilation and temperature regulation)
findings.consequent: Use of air conditioning and heating systems, energy consumption, utility bills
findings.quote: For example, buildings that mimic termite mounds for natural ventilation and temperature regulation can significantly cut down on the use of air conditioning and heating systems, leading to lower energy consumption and reduced utility bills.

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (lotus leaf inspired self-cleaning surfaces)
findings.consequent: Need for frequent cleaning and maintenance
findings.quote: For instance, self-cleaning surfaces inspired by the lotus leaf can reduce the need for frequent cleaning and maintenance (Finsterwalde, 2011).

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (efficient use of materials)
findings.quote: Biomimicry encourages the use of materials in a way that mimics the efficiency of natural systems, often leading to less waste during construction (Al-Ketan et al., 2022). This efficient use of materials can reduce the overall material costs and waste management expenses.

findings.antecedent: Reduced HVAC use (due to biomimetic designs)
findings.quote: The energy savings from reduced HVAC use can be substantial, often reducing energy consumption by 30-50% compared to conventional buildings.

findings.antecedent: Biomimicry (mimicking natural resilience)
findings.quote: By mimicking the resilience of natural systems, biomimetic buildings can be more durable and require fewer repairs over time (Gruber, 2011).

findings.antecedent: Enhanced indoor air quality and natural light
findings.consequent: Occupant health, productivity, healthcare costs, overall productivity in commercial settings
findings.quote: Enhanced indoor air quality and natural light can improve occupant health and productivity, potentially reducing costs associated with healthcare and increasing the overall productivity in commercial settings (Al Horr et al., 2016).

findings.antecedent: Healthier environments
findings.quote: Healthier environments also tend to have lower turnover rates and absenteeism.

findings.antecedent: Innovative biomimetic designs and improved indoor air quality
findings.consequent: Attractiveness to tenants/buyers, occupancy rates, rental incomes
findings.quote: Buildings with innovative biomimetic designs and improved indoor air quality are often more attractive to tenants and buyers, leading to higher occupancy rates and potentially higher rental incomes.
